bio.summary: Marquis is a sitting councilmember seeking a second term. Her priorities include family housing, homelessness, wildfire resilience and accountable government.
bio.public_office: Boulder city councilmember, elected 2023; previously BVSD school board

statements.text: The city is working toward outcome-based budgeting.
statements.speaker: Tina Marquis

statements.text: I made extensive comments about the DDA at the council meeting when I voted against the DDA at this time.
statements.speaker: Tina Marquis

statements.text: I made extensive comments about the DDA at the council meeting when I voted against the DDA.
statements.speaker: Tina Marquis
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Tina Marquis

statements.text: Marquis voted against sending the DDA proposal to DDA voters, and noted that she didn’t believe there was sufficient community “buy-in,” in part because of a “compressed timeline” and not enough input from other entities with approved dedicated tax revenues that might have lost funding through tax-increment financing arrangements.
statements.speaker: Richard Valenty reporting Tina Marquis’s interview

statements.text: In general, I try to be accessible to all constituents through email, phone or in-person meetings, though recognize there are times when I cannot respond to all requests in a short window.
statements.speaker: Tina Marquis
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Tina Marquis

statements.text: No. While I did vote no in 2025, I did support allowing duplexes and triplexes in more areas during the comp plan process.
statements.speaker: Tina Marquis

statements.text: When I first ran three years ago, public safety was perhaps the biggest issue during the campaign.
statements.speaker: Tina Marquis
statements.source_title: 2026 Mayoral and City Council Candidate Questions — Tina Marquis

forum_quotes.question: If elected, name your top three priorities. And do you believe the city is moving in the right direction or wrong direction on those top priorities?
forum_quotes.quote: Trying to find more middle income housing, making sure that our climate is resilient, working hard on safety, including safety from wildfire
caveats: Quoted from an automatic transcript. Check the recording.
forum_quotes.recording_title: 2026 | Boulder City Council Candidate Forum (Boulder Chamber, YouTube)

forum_quotes.forum_name: Boulder Chamber City Council and Mayoral Candidate Forum
forum_quotes.question: What role do you see public and private partnerships playing in some of our greatest areas of need?
forum_quotes.quote: we identified a problem with our unsheltered homeless population and looked to see how we could support them and also maintain our public safety goals.
caveats: Quoted from an automatic transcript. Check the recording.
Transcript note: Moderator called 'Lynn, and then Tina' (garbled in the transcript; confirmed by a listener).
